R7AB-bear-atv-0001.name: By Meadows Creek
R7AB-bear-atv-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R7AB-bear-atv-0001.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Big602); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2008 (18 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2018 (fire C12330), 470 m N: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Meadows Creek 50 m W: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from City of Prince George, about 137 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Carney St, Hwy 16, Hwy 97, Hwy 97 (Cariboo Hwy).

Ride: 3.2 km on A20013-523, A20013 Cp 551 by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 90 m E, climb about 0 m.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-15, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.

evidence.t: Trail: Stoney Lake Trails, 5.2 km stretch.
100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
8 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
15 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.
